title: Asia stocks mixed as Apple outlook weighs; RBA raises rates to 18-yr high
full_text:
Investing.com-- Asian stocks were mixed on Tuesday as investors assessed Apple's earnings outlook and positioned for the U.S. midterm elections, while the Reserve Bank of Australia raised interest rates for the fifth time this year to curb persistent inflation.
The moves followed losses on Wall Street, where the S&P 500 fell 0.5% on Monday, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.1%, as weakness in technology shares weighed on sentiment.

Traders weigh Apple results; KOSPI falls 3%
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) shares came under pressure after the iPhone maker forecast lower gross margins for the crucial holiday quarter, citing rising memory-chip costs, and projected services revenue growth that fell short of Wall Street expectations.
The company's outlook added to concerns over the cost and profitability of technology investment, with investors also assessing whether heavy spending on artificial intelligence will deliver sufficient returns.
U.S. stock futures edged higher in Asian trading, but investors remained cautious ahead of Tuesday's midterm elections, which could reshape the balance of power in Congress and affect President Donald Trump's policy agenda.
South Korea's KOSPI led declines in Asia, with the benchmark dropping more than 3%.
China's Shanghai Composite slipped 0.8%, while the blue-chip Shanghai Shenzhen CSI 300 edged down 0.2%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng traded 0.5% higher.
Japanese markets were closed for a public holiday.
Singapore's Straits Times Index fell 0.3%, while India's Nifty 50 gained 0.7%.
RBA hikes rates to 18-yr high
Australia's S&P/ASX 200 rose 0.4% after the Reserve Bank raised its cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.85%, its highest level since 2008, as inflation remained stubbornly high.
The decision marked the fifth rate increase this year and came amid concerns that elevated energy costs and domestic price pressures could keep inflation above target.
The decision was split, with six board members voting for a hike and three preferring to leave rates unchanged.
In China, the People's Bank of China said it would raise the foreign exchange deposit reserve ratio for financial institutions to 6% from 4%, effective November 15, in a move aimed at strengthening management of foreign exchange liquidity.
Investors were also watching developments in the Middle East after oil prices fell more than 7% on Monday on hopes for progress in U.S.-Iran peace talks.
However, a Wall Street Journal report said that the U.S. attacked Iran's Qeshm Island on Monday.

title: Oil rises after reported U.S. strike on Iran’s Qeshm Island
full_text:
Investing.com-- Oil prices edged higher in Asian trading Tuesday after falling sharply in the previous session, as a reported U.S. strike on Iran's Qeshm Island revived concerns about Middle East supply disruptions.
As of 20:22 ET (01:22 GMT), Brent Oil Futures expiring in January rose 0.3% to $105.4 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures gained 0.5% to $96.93 per barrel.
Get premium commodity market insights with InvestingPro
The United States attacked Iran's Qeshm Island on Monday, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing U.S. officials.
The strike was part of a series of limited U.S. attacks on Iran in recent weeks, the report said, as Washington sought to avoid signalling a return to a broader military campaign. Qeshm lies in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil shipments.
The reported attack highlighted the fragile balance between military escalation and diplomatic efforts to end the conflict, keeping traders alert to the risk of further disruption to oil flows through the Gulf.
Crude prices had slumped on Monday after U.S. officials signalled a preference for negotiations, easing concerns that Washington could resume a wider military campaign following Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Tehran was willing to pursue dialogue, while Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said discussions with Qatari mediators were continuing. The talks have focused on a possible framework to end the conflict and restore stability to the region.
However, the diplomatic signals have yet to produce a durable agreement, leaving uncertainty over the future of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
The United States and Iran have also exchanged conflicting signals over the possibility of renewed military action. Trump said on Monday he did not intend to strike Iran after Tuesday's midterm elections, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has reportedly urged Washington to resume attacks.

title: Apple suppliers split in Asia as strong iPhone sales meet rising memory costs
full_text:
Investing.com -- Shares of Apple-linked suppliers traded unevenly across Asia on Tuesday, with South Korean component and memory-chip makers falling while some Chinese manufacturers advanced.
Investors weighed stronger iPhone demand against rising component costs and mixed earnings across the supply chain.
In an early-session, LG Innotek fell 4.6%, SK Hynix dropped 3.5% and Samsung Electronics lost 3.3%. Taiwan’s Largan Precision declined 4.2%.
By contrast, China’s Goertek gained 2.7% and Luxshare Precision rose 0.6%. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. was little changed.
Get InvestingPro at 55% off and stay ahead of market moves
Apple’s latest results offered mixed signals for suppliers. September-quarter iPhone revenue jumped 17.5% year on year to $57.6 billion, driven by strong iPhone 18 Pro demand, helping lift overall revenue above expectations.
However, Apple forecast December-quarter gross margin of 45%-46%, down from 47.9% previously, as rising memory costs weigh on profitability. iPad and wearables sales also disappointed, while services growth is expected to slow.
Apple’s suppliers also logged a mixed batch of September quarter earnings in recent weeks.
South Korean camera-module supplier LG Innotek reported an 18.6% rise in third-quarter revenue, but operating profit plunged 53.4% as currency movements squeezed margins.
It bought raw materials when the won was weaker against the dollar but shipped products after the currency strengthened. Revenue at its optical solutions division, which includes camera modules, still rose 20.6%.
Taiwan’s Largan Precision also faced margin pressure, with revenue falling 11.5% and net profit declining 27.7%. Gross margin dropped to a 13-year low of 42.21%, hit by lower yields on new smartphone camera lenses and higher energy costs.
Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix fell despite record quarterly earnings, supported by AI-related memory demand and strong sales of high-bandwidth memory and server products. Both had rallied in the previous session, potentially leaving room for profit-taking.
Chinese suppliers were more mixed. Goertek recorded modest increases in nine-month revenue and profit, while Luxshare Precision reported year-on-year growth in third-quarter revenue and net profit. Luxshare’s nine-month revenue climbed 29%, with attributable net profit up 13.4%.

title: RBA hikes interest rates to 2008 levels, sharply raises inflation forecasts
full_text:
Investing.com-- The Reserve Bank of Australia raised interest rates to a 18-year high on Tuesday and sharply hiked its inflation expectations for the year, warning of more rate increases.
The RBA hiked its cash rate target by 25 basis points to 4.85%, in line with market expectations. The decision was not unanimous, with three of the RBA’s nine-member rate-setting board voting in favor of a hold.
The cash rate is now at its highest level since late-2008, where the RBA had aggressively hiked rates in the wake of the global financial crisis.
Tuesday’s hike is the RBA’s fifth such move this year, and comes as the central bank struggles to quash sticky Australian inflation. A mix of higher energy prices– due to the Middle East conflict– plus strong domestic demand and artificial intelligence investment drove Australian consumer price index inflation to near three-year highs this year.
Core inflation, as measured by trimmed mean CPI, also sat well above the RBA’s 2% to 3% target range.
The RBA hiked its end-2026 CPI forecast to 4.7% from a prior forecast of 3.6%. Trimmed mean CPI is expected at 3.6%, up from prior forecasts of 3.3%.
“Given the revised inflation outlook and the continuing upside risks, the Board judged that a further tightening in financial conditions is warranted to support the return of inflation to target,” the RBA said in a statement.
“Monetary policy is well placed to respond to developments, and the Board is focused on its mandate to deliver price stability and full employment.”
The central bank flagged increasing risks that higher inflation expectations will become embedded– a scenario the RBA has constantly warned against.
Still, the RBA hiked its gross domestic product forecast for 2026, to 1.6% from 1.4%.
The RBA raised its unemployment forecast to 4.7% from 4.5% by end-2026, flagging some cooling in the economy due to high rates.
The Australian dollar weakened slightly after the RBA’s hike, with the AUD/USD pair falling 0.2%.
Capital Economics analysts said Tuesday’s move showed the RBA as more confident that monetary policy was sufficiently tight, and that the central bank’s next move would be a cut.

title: China hikes forex deposit reserve ratio to 6%
full_text:
Investing.com-- The People’s Bank of China said on Tuesday it will raise the foreign exchange deposit reserve ratio for local institutions to 6% from 4%, starting November 15.
The hike is aimed at strengthening foreign exchange liquidity management by local institutions, the PBOC said in a statement.
The FX deposit reserve ratio determines the amount of dollar reserves local financial institutions are mandated to keep with the PBOC. An increase in the ratio will require local institutions to lock up an additional 2% of their dollar reserves with the central bank-- tightening domestic dollar supplies and increasing yuan liquidity.
Such a move is negative for the Chinese currency.

Tuesday’s move indicates some discomfort in Beijing over recent strength in the yuan, which surged to an over four-year high in October.
A stronger yuan stands to pressure Chinese exports, which are the country’s main economic engine. The yuan rose sharply this year following a string of stronger midpoint fixes from the PBOC.
The Chinese yuan weakened on Tuesday following the PBOC’s move. The USD/CNY pair, which gauges the number of yuan required to purchase on dollar, rose 0.3% to 6.6706.
The pair had touched its lowest level in four years in October, following a series of strong midpoint fixings by the PBOC. The yuan is only allowed to move within 2% margin of a midpoint set by the PBOC on a daily basis.
Beijing has faced increasing pressure from major trading partners to strengthen the yuan, amid increasing accusations of overseas dumping by Chinese companies. A softer yuan stands to make Chinese exports less competitive in overseas markets.

title: Reddit blasts Australia’s ’inept’ social media ban as court challenge begins
full_text:
By Peter Hobson
CANBERRA, Nov 3 (Reuters) - Australia’s world-first teen social media ban was "ill thought out" and amounted to a "profound restriction on political debate", a lawyer for messaging platform Reddit told the country’s top court in the first legal challenge to the law.
Reddit and a libertarian advocacy group have taken to the High Court to contest the Australian law, which bans large social media platforms from letting under-16s have an account and took effect in late 2025 amid support from parents and opposition from the tech firms.
A successful challenge could usher in more opposition from affected companies and slow a global uptake of similar policies as lawmakers from Britain to Malaysia roll out the measures in an effort to protect youth mental and physical health.
The Australian government and its communications minister, a named defendant, have said they will defend the law.
Addressing the court, Perry Herzfeld, for Reddit, said barring under-16s from holding social media accounts stopped them from creating or responding to content on what he called the most important means of communication in the modern world.
"That is a very profound restriction on political debate in Australia," Herzfeld said.
"There is a very substantial restriction on what young people can now do."
Reddit agreed with the Australians’ harm-minimisation aim but the law failed to do so, Herzfeld said, terming the legislation "ill thought out" and "inept" since it did not call for any specific measure to keep out minors and failed to restrict other online services where cyberbullying took place, such as gaming websites.
While social media content could typically only be created or commented on by logged-in account-holders, vast amounts of material were visible to people with no account, he said.
"If the Commonwealth is worried about particular features (of social media), it should regulate the features, which it has not done," he said.
Since the ban went live, multiple studies, including by Australian regulator the eSafety Commissioner, have found that most of the country’s teenagers under the cutoff age continue to use social media.
The government has since doubled the maximum fine for non-compliance to A$99 million ($69.5 million), given the eSafety Commissioner greater discovery powers, and said it is preparing an enforcement lawsuit against some of the biggest platforms.
($1 = 1.4253 Australian dollars)

title: European shares slide as Apple margin warning trigger global tech rout
full_text:
Investing.com - European shares dropped on Tuesday, succumbing to a worldwide sell-off across technology bourses after Apple warned of margin compression from rising chip costs, while a $20 billion capital raise by Oracle reignited investor anxiety over artificial intelligence funding and cash burn.
The pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 0.7%, while Germany’s DAX fell nearly 1%. France’s CAC 40 fell 0.5% while London’s FTSE 100 fell 0.4%. Italy’s FTSE MIB and Spain’s IBEX 35 dropped over 1% each.
The drawdown was led by the technology sector after Apple warned that persistent inflation in memory chip prices would squeeze gross margins through the crucial holiday shopping quarter.
The continent’s semiconductor ecosystem - including lithography giant ASML, assembly equipment makers ASM International and BE SemiconductoR all fell between 2% and 4% and chip suppliers STMicroelectronics and Infineon - trades as a direct proxy for global consumer electronics hardware and datacenter supply chains - fell over 3% each.
With the world’s most valuable tech platform signaling that higher component bills are eroding profitability, European semiconductor suppliers came under sharp selling pressure amid fears that hardware makers will either absorb margin compression or face demand destruction if input expenses are passed on to consumers
The hardware chill was compounded by news that enterprise software giant Oracle plans to raise $20 billion through a combination of bond and share sales to fund its aggressive cloud infrastructure and datacenter expansion.
This week, about 20% of the STOXX 600 companies are expected to report their quarterly results, marking one of the busiest stretches of the European third-quarter earnings season.
German airline group Lufthansa saw its shares gain 1.6%. The management narrowed its full-year 2026 operating profit forecast due to soaring jet fuel costs tied to Middle Eastern supply tensions.
Conversely, Dutch medical technology heavyweight Koninklijke Philips advanced 6.4% after posting higher quarterly profit.
U.S. midterms test Trump’s second-term agenda
Cross-asset flows were further restrained by caution ahead of Tuesday’s U.S. midterm elections, with American voters heading to the polls to deliver a referendum on the first two years of President Donald Trump’s second term.
A Democratic-controlled or divided Congress would introduce legislative gridlock, slowing domestic deregulatory momentum and raising the stakes for upcoming federal debt ceiling negotiations, while potentially curbing federal spending initiatives.
With investors also awaiting Friday’s October U.S. nonfarm payrolls report to gauge the Federal Reserve’s December interest-rate trajectory, dealing desks maintained low risk profiles across European bourses.

title: Gold holds near $3,950 as Iran peace hopes ease oil, U.S. vote in focus
full_text:
Investing.com -- Gold prices fell on Tuesday, giving back ground after earlier rebound as renewed selling across precious metals kept bullion under pressure, with spot gold slipping below $3,950 an ounce.
At 00:55 ET (05:55 GMT), spot gold fell 0.7% to $3,920.44 an ounce, while U.S. gold futures declined 1% to $3,929.67. Silver dropped 2.8% to $49.2455 an ounce, while platinum lost 1% to $1,432.32. Spot palladium fell 1.6% to $952.15, while palladium futures declined 1.9% to $944.00. The U.S. dollar Index slipped marginally by 0.1% to 101.75.
Bullion climbed 1.9% on Monday after Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said his government had received greater authority from the country’s supreme leader to pursue peace negotiations.
U.S. President Donald Trump also indicated progress in the discussions, helping Brent crude fall more than 7% before oil prices stabilised on Tuesday.
The nine-month U.S.-Iran conflict has driven energy prices higher and fuelled inflation, increasing pressure on central banks to raise interest rates.
Higher borrowing costs typically weigh on gold because it does not generate interest income. However, easing oil prices have temporarily reduced concerns about further monetary tightening.
Gold fell 6.8% in October, breaking below the key $4,000 threshold toward the end of the month and reaching a one-year low.
The metal also suffered from last week’s retreat in artificial intelligence-related stocks, as investors liquidated bullion holdings to cover losses elsewhere. Further weakness in Asian technology shares on Tuesday, following a deeper selloff in U.S. chipmakers, left gold vulnerable to additional selling.
The U.S. midterm elections could provide another catalyst, with results potentially influencing gold prices during Wednesday’s Asian session. Investors are assessing whether a shift in the political landscape could refocus attention on U.S. inflation and fiscal deficits, potentially restoring bullion’s appeal as a hedge against economic and geopolitical uncertainty.
Technical indicators also offered some support, with a measure of gold’s relative strength moving into oversold territory last week, suggesting prices could be poised for a recovery. Physical demand has provided another source of support, according to ANZ, particularly from Chinese households that have stepped up purchases during the recent price decline.
Despite the recent rebound, renewed fighting in the Middle East remains a risk, particularly as hopes for diplomatic progress could quickly reverse.

title: Philips Q3 adjusted earnings rise as order intake strengthens
full_text:
Investing.com-- Koninklijke Philips (AS:PHG) shares climbed to an eight-month high on Tuesday after the Dutch health technology company reported stronger third-quarter adjusted earnings, supported by improved margins and robust order growth.
Shares rose 3.22% to €25.31, touching their highest level since March 5 and sharply outperforming the broader AEX index, which fell 0.2%.
Get real-time earnings updates with InvestingPro subscription
Philips reported third-quarter comparable sales growth of 3% to €4.39 billion, around 40 basis points below company-compiled analyst consensus. Adjusted EBITA, however, increased 7.2% year on year to €569 million, beating consensus by around 9%. The adjusted EBITA margin expanded 70 basis points to 13%.
Comparable order intake increased 8%, driven by strong demand in Diagnosis & Treatment, where orders grew at a rate approaching 20%, with double-digit growth in both Image Guided Therapy and Precision Diagnosis, Citi said.
However, sales in the division were flat, as growth in Image Guided Therapy was offset by weaker Precision Diagnosis revenue. Connected Care recorded 5% comparable sales growth, while Personal Health increased 8%.
Citi described the quarter as mixed, noting that adjusted EBITA performance and Connected Care were stronger than expected. Although, it warned that sluggish Diagnosis & Treatment sales momentum raised questions about Philips’ ability to achieve its 2027 and medium-term growth ambitions.
The bank also noted that Philips’ 8% group order growth compared with 4% at GE HealthCare in the quarter, although its four-year cumulative order growth of 1.5% remained below GE HealthCare’s 3%.
Net income fell to €28 million from €187 million a year earlier, reflecting a €288 million provision linked to an agreement in principle with the U.S. Department of Justice to resolve criminal and civil investigations related to the Respironics recall.
Philips reiterated its 2026 outlook, including comparable sales growth of 3% to 4.5%, an adjusted EBITA margin of 13.5% to 14% and free cash flow of €1.5 billion to €1.7 billion.

title: Stocks slip as AI jitters, US midterms keep investors on edge
full_text:
By Niket Nishant and Gregor Stuart Hunter
Nov 3 (Reuters) - A fresh bout of AI anxiety pressured global stocks on Tuesday, while investors were on tenterhooks as voting began in crucial US midterm elections.
Traders on Polymarket see about a 77% chance of Democrats winning both chambers of the US Congress, an outcome that could lead to tougher oversight of AI and more corporate regulation.
"In the case of a full blue sweep, I would expect some populist measures against AI. The narrative against data centres would get a tailwind," said Alexander Lis, chief investment officer at Social Discovery Ventures.
Big Tech’s lacklustre earnings and steep capital spending targets have unnerved Wall Street in recent days, putting the election verdict under greater scrutiny.
Futures tracking the tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 index were broadly flat while S&P 500 contracts dropped 0.14%. The indexes fell for a third straight session on Monday.
The pan-European STOXX 600 index was down 0.6% to 645.36 points. South Korea’s KOSPI benchmark fell 3.6%, while Taiwan’s index dropped 3.6% for its steepest one-day decline since late July.
MSCI’s gauge of stocks across the globe slipped 0.26%.
The dollar index, which measures the currency against a basket of peers, dipped to 101.69. It hit a one-month low on Monday.
The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note rose 1.2 basis points to 4.9064%.
A surprise Republican sweep would likely lift yields and the dollar, said Steve Englander, co-head of FX research at Standard Chartered.
OIL VOLATILE, APPLE ADDS TO EARNINGS ANGST

title: Bayer shares jump 5% as Q3 beat prompts 2026 forecast upgrade
full_text:
Investing.com -- Shares in Bayer (ETR:BAYGn) rose more than 5% on Tuesday after the German healthcare and agriculture group raised its full-year earnings and cash flow forecasts, following third-quarter sales and EBITDA that beat analyst expectations on strong growth in its pharmaceuticals division.
The German healthcare and agriculture group now expects 2026 EBITDA before special items of €9.8 billion to €10.3 billion on a currency-adjusted basis, compared with its previous forecast of €9.6 billion to €10.1 billion.
Third-quarter group sales rose 4.1% to €10.05 billion from €9.66 billion a year earlier, beating the €9.92 billion consensus compiled by Vara Research.
EBITDA before special items increased 6.9% to €1.62 billion from €1.51 billion, above analyst expectations of €1.43 billion.
The pharmaceuticals division drove the growth, with sales rising 8% to €4.68 billion and EBITDA before special items increasing 23.6% to €1.29 billion from €1.05 billion.
Net loss narrowed to €672 million from €963 million a year earlier, but was wider than the €242 million loss expected by analysts. The result included a €307 million impairment charge on the Xofigo brand in the pharmaceuticals division and €407 million in special charges.
Core earnings per share fell to a loss of €0.31 from earnings of €0.49 a year earlier, missing the €0.36 consensus, partly due to non-cash charges related to interest rate changes.
Free cash flow fell to a negative €293 million from positive €596 million a year earlier, partly reflecting expected higher payments to resolve legal proceedings.
Net financial debt declined to €31.08 billion from €32.71 billion a year earlier, largely due to a €3 billion payment from Apollo Global Management.
Chief Executive Bill Anderson said the pharmaceuticals division had reached a turning point in its growth trajectory.
Chief Financial Officer Judith Hartmann said the company’s year-to-date performance gave it confidence to raise its full-year earnings, cash flow and debt targets.
Bayer also raised its 2026 free cash flow forecast to between negative €1.5 billion and negative €0.5 billion, from negative €2.5 billion to negative €1.5 billion previously.
It now expects year-end net financial debt of €28 billion to €29 billion, compared with its previous forecast of €29 billion to €30 billion.
The company raised its full-year EBITDA margin forecast for the pharmaceuticals division to 25% to 27% from 23% to 25%.

title: Asian currencies mixed as Aussie falls after RBA hike, yuan weakens
full_text:
Investing.com -- Asian currencies traded mixed on Tuesday, with the Australian dollar weakening despite a widely expected rate hike from the Reserve Bank of Australia, while the South Korean won strengthened and the Chinese yuan retreated after a policy move by its central bank.
The U.S. dollar index fell 0.12% to 101.69. The Australian dollar slipped 0.2% to $0.6988, while the South Korean won strengthened 0.5% to 1,339.37 per dollar.
The offshore yuan weakened 0.37% to 6.6710 per dollar and its onshore counterpart fell 0.38% to 6.6731. The Taiwan dollar was among the weaker regional currencies, falling 0.6% against the greenback, while the Philippine peso and Indonesian rupiah lost 0.34% and 0.4%, respectively.
The Singapore dollar and Malaysian ringgit also weakened, while the Indian rupee was little changed at 94.918 per dollar. The yen edged higher to 157.80 per dollar in holiday-thinned Japanese trading. The New Zealand dollar gained 0.1% to $0.5629, while the euro and sterling rose 0.13% and 0.1%, respectively.
Australian dollar slips as split RBA decision points to a policy pause
The RBA raised its cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.85%, its highest level in 18 years and its fifth increase this year. However, the 6-3 vote was less unanimous than markets had anticipated, with three of the nine board members favouring an unchanged rate.
The Australian dollar fell as much as 0.4% after the decision. Capital Economics economist Marcel Thieliant said the RBA appeared more confident that policy was sufficiently tight, noting that it now described financial conditions as “restrictive” rather than “somewhat restrictive.”
The firm expects the bank to have finished raising rates, with its next move likely to be a cut, although not until late 2027.
The RBA nevertheless raised its inflation outlook, projecting trimmed mean inflation at 3.5% by mid-2027, up from its previous forecast of 3.0%. It cited higher fuel and commodity costs linked to the Middle East conflict, as well as tighter domestic capacity pressures.
The dollar also struggled to benefit from broader risk aversion. Investors are weighing Tuesday’s U.S. midterm elections and Friday’s employment report.
DBS expects October nonfarm payrolls to increase by 100,000, compared with 29,000 previously, with the data potentially influencing whether the Fed reconsiders its tightening bias.
Yuan retreats after PBOC move as won draws support from exports
The offshore yuan weakened after the People’s Bank of China announced it would raise the foreign-exchange reserve requirement ratio by two percentage points to 6% from 4%, effective November 15.
The adjustment is expected to withdraw around $24 billion from the financial system by absorbing dollar liquidity. The move aims to slow the yuan’s appreciation after gains of more than 5% against the dollar this year, supported by strong exports, trade surpluses and corporate currency conversions.
The won’s latest advance comes after it gained around 13% against the dollar in the third quarter, its strongest quarterly rise since late 1998.
South Korea’s October exports surged 93.7% year-on-year to a record $115.28 billion, the fastest growth since January 1974, as semiconductor shipments jumped 259.4%. Inflation eased to 2.8% from 2.9%, but remained above the Bank of Korea’s 2% target.
The remaining regional calendar includes Bank Negara Malaysia’s rate decision on Thursday, where DBS expects the policy rate to remain at 2.75%, alongside October inflation readings from Taiwan, Thailand and the Philippines.

title: TeamViewer shares plunge 19% after Q3 revenue fall, 2026 outlook cut
full_text:
Investing.com -- Shares in TeamViewer crashed 19% on Tuesday after the German software maker cut its 2026 revenue growth forecast following a third-quarter decline in revenue and annual recurring revenue, citing slower enterprise deal conversions and continued economic weakness in Europe.
The German software maker now expects 2026 revenue growth of between -2% and -1% at constant currencies, compared with its previous forecast of 0% to 3%, against pro forma revenue of €767.5 million in 2025. It reaffirmed its adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of around 43%.
Third-quarter revenue fell 3.9% to €184.5 million from €192 million a year earlier. Annual recurring revenue (ARR) declined 2.6% to €736.9 million from €756.8 million.
Adjusted EBITDA fell 10% to €78.9 million from €87.7 million, with the margin narrowing to 42.8% from 45.7%. Net income, however, rose 26% to €36 million from €28.7 million.
Chief executive Oliver Steil said enterprise deal conversions remained too slow and customer retention too low, weighing on the fourth-quarter outlook.
He said the company needed to strengthen and expand its global enterprise sales organisation.
Steil said TeamViewer had seen continued momentum in new business, growth in ARR among its largest enterprise customers and signs of stabilisation in its small and medium-sized business segment. He expressed confidence in accelerating growth in 2027 and beyond.
Chief revenue officer Mark Banfield said TeamViewer ONE accounted for around 10% of enterprise ARR less than a year after its launch, driven by new customer wins and upgrades from existing clients.
He said the U.S. enterprise business was a particular source of strength in the third quarter, but uncertainty over U.S. federal budgets was expected to delay the conversion of large public-sector deals in the pipeline.
Banfield also cited customer AkzoNobel, which has used TeamViewer’s DEX software to automate IT support across more than 25,000 devices, cutting support tickets by more than 40%.
Chief Financial Officer Michael Wilkens said the company maintained an adjusted EBITDA margin of 42.8%, in line with its full-year guidance, despite weaker revenue. Levered free cash flow increased 29% year-on-year.
TeamViewer also completed refinancing measures during the quarter, extending debt maturities, diversifying funding sources and fully repaying the bridge facility used for its 1E acquisition.
The company said it remained focused on improving customer retention, investing in sales and research and development, and reducing leverage.

title: Abu Dhabi’s XRG to acquire Shell’s stake in Australian LNG project
full_text:
Investing.com -- Abu Dhabi’s XRG will purchase Shell’s stake in the Woodside Energy-operated North West Shelf project for $1.45 billion, marking the ADNOC subsidiary’s first asset in Australia.
The transaction involves a 16.67% non-operated interest in the North West Shelf project, one of Australia’s largest liquefied natural gas export facilities.
The project comprises several interconnected joint ventures involving Woodside, Chevron, BP, Shell, China’s CNOOC, and Japan LNG, which includes Mitsui and Mitsubishi.
The sale is expected to close in 2027. Shell stated the deal includes an additional milestone-linked contingent payment on top of the base consideration. XRG will assume all decommissioning obligations under the agreement.
XRG recently established two local holding companies in Australia, registered with the Australian Securities and Investments Commission.
In 2025, the Abu Dhabi-based company made an on-market offer for Australia’s Santos for $18.7 billion, which it terminated in mid-September after failing to agree on commercial terms.
Woodside announced in its third-quarter results late last month that it plans to shut a second train at the North West Shelf facility in 2027.
The shutdown comes as production declines from legacy fields and the facility seeks more third-party gas to process until the Browse fields come online.
Shell said it continues to invest in LNG and integrated gas globally and will grow LNG sales by 4-5% per year to 2030.

title: Lufthansa cuts 2026 outlook as jet fuel bill hits €9.3 billion
full_text:
By Joanna Plucinska and Ilona Wissenbach
LONDON, Nov 3 (Reuters) - Lufthansa trimmed its profit outlook on Tuesday as the German airline’s estimated jet fuel bill for 2026 rose to €9.3 billion, although its third-quarter results were in line with forecasts.
European carriers have warned that the rising cost of jet fuel resulting from the Iran war will weigh on their outlooks, with ticket prices set to rise next year as hedges expire.
Bernstein analyst Alex Irving said the more resilient results show Lufthansa’s turnaround programme may be starting to bear fruit despite the challenging fuel environment.
Lufthansa shares were up 1.5% soon after markets opened.
"With rising revenues amid consistently high demand and strict cost discipline, we were able to more than offset the increase in fuel costs of approximately half a billion euros," Lufthansa CEO Carsten Spohr said in a statement.
The German airline group said its total fuel costs rose by more than €400 million ($448 million) compared to last year.
Lufthansa trimmed its operating profit forecast for the 2026 financial year to between €1.7 billion and €2 billion, compared to an earlier €1.7 billion to €2.2 billion range.
It also confirmed capacity growth for the year was expected to be flat as it posted a €1.4 billion operating profit for its third quarter, which is usually the most profitable for European airlines because it includes the peak summer season.
That compared to a company-compiled analyst projection of €1.37 billion.
Chief Financial Officer Till Streichert said the full-year operating profit would depend on demand, fuel costs and the performance of Lufthansa Cargo in the fourth quarter.
The airline group said it saw considerable demand in its premium segment, reflecting a trend that major network carriers have flagged. It added that traffic to Asia and North America was also strong, helping to drive resilience.
